item.title: Trump raises concerns in call with Rep. Max Miller amid abuse allegations
item.description: Ohio Rep. Max Miller's reelection campaign has been upended by allegations that Miller assaulted his ex-wife, Emily Moreno, and their 2-year-old daughter.

item.title: Sen. Moreno says ex-son-in-law Max Miller shouldn't serve in Congress
item.description: GOP Sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio said his former son-in-law, Rep. Max Miller, shouldn't serve in Congress amid swirling abuse claims, as Miller vowed to stay in the race for another term and strongly denied all allegations of misconduct.

item.title: No new Iran negotiations planned despite Trump comments, U.S. officials say
item.description: President Trump, who called Tehran "unbelievably duplicitous," said the talks are the "last chance" for Iran to forge a deal and avoid an escalation.

item.title: 8/3: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Trump says he's giving Iran a "last chance" at diplomacy; Blanche one step closer to confirmation as attorney general.

item.title: Trump says Jeanine Pirro "choked" in dropping Reflecting Pool cases
item.description: "She folded like an umbrella," President Trump said of Jeanine Pirro, U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.

item.title: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" continues Hollywood's hot streak at the box office
item.description: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" leapt straight to the top of the box office this weekend. Its $360 million opening weekend debut is the biggest in U.S. history. Marlow Stern, chief correspondent at Variety, joins CBS News to discuss all the latest movie news.

item.title: Most federal workers say they wouldn't enter public service again, survey finds
item.description: According to the National Active and Retired Federal Employees Association, 64% of workers say it's unlikely they would choose a federal career again. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: Latest on In-N-Out Idaho shooting that killed 3 as police search for motive
item.description: Three people were killed by a 24-year-old gunman at an In-N-Out in Twin Falls, Idaho, on Saturday. Lilia Luciano breaks down what we know.

item.title: Twin Falls In-N-Out shooting suspect identified after 3 killed, 7 wounded
item.description: The suspect, identified as 24-year-old Chad Williams, died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, police said.

item.title: How do AI developers move forward after OpenAI hacking incident?
item.description: Matt Shumer, CBS News AI contributor, shares his thoughts on last month's incident where a rogue OpenAI model that was being tested hacked an outside company's data processing system.

item.title: Rep. Haley Stevens on Israel, the Democratic Party and PAC money
item.description: Democratic Senate candidate Rep. Haley Stevens speaks with CBS News' Ed O'Keefe about the Democratic Party, PAC donations and Israel as her primary race with Dr. Abdul El-Sayed comes down to the wire.

item.title: More Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool charges dropped by Pirro's office
item.description: Since Friday, D.C. U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro's office has dropped charges against three more people accused of vandalism.

item.title: Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie case contradicted himself on ransom note
item.description: Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos told CBS News last Thursday that he didn't have a ransom note saying Nancy Guthrie was dead. But one day later he released a note saying just that. CBS News' Anna Schecter reports.

item.title: Ariana Grande pulls out of musical over "endless, ongoing public scrutiny"
item.description: Ariana Grande had been due to star alongside her "Wicked" co-star Jonathan Bailey in a production of "Sunday in the Park with George" in 2027.

item.title: "My Favorite Person" trend making social media users tear up
item.description: A social media trend encouraging users to share what they love about their favorite person is bringing light to TikTok and other platforms.

item.title: Ariana Grande to step out of public eye amid "scrutiny," drops out of London musical
item.description: A representative for pop star Ariana Grande says the singer is planning to step out of the public eye after wrapping her ongoing Eternal Sunshine Tour amid "endless, ongoing public scrutiny." Grande has also dropped out of the London-based musical "Sunday in the Park with George," which is set to open next year.

item.title: "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" debuts with biggest domestic opening weekend ever
item.description: At the box office, "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" swung to a massive $360 million in its domestic debut, making it the biggest opening weekend ever. Brooks Barnes, chief Hollywood correspondent for The New York Times, joins to discuss.

item.title: Michigan reports 2 deaths in cyclosporiasis outbreak
item.description: Health officials in Michigan have reported two deaths related to a nationwide cyclosporiasis outbreak. CBS News correspondent Carter Evans has the latest.

item.title: New details in Idaho In-N-Out shooting, two people returned fire against gunman
item.description: New information is coming out about the shooting at an In-N-Out restaurant in Idaho that killed three people over the weekend. CBS News' Lilia Luciano reports.

item.title: Cornyn, Tillis back Blanche for attorney general after deal on DOJ fund
item.description: GOP Sens. John Cornyn of Texas and Thom Tillis of North Carolina formally announced their support on Monday for Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general.

item.title: More young adults moving back home with their parents amid affordability crisis
item.description: Rising prices and affordability issues are forcing more young adults to move back in with their parents. Jericka Duncan has the story.

item.title: Senate candidate El-Sayed questions assumption Michigan voters are moderates
item.description: Populist Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens top the Democratic field going into Tuesday's Senate primary. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is running unopposed for the GOP nomination.

item.title: El-Sayed and Stevens make final pitches before Democratic Michigan Senate primary
item.description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens are in the final throws of their Democratic Senate primary in Michigan. CBS News' Aaron Navarro reports.

item.title: Washington wildfires leave some residents with nothing: "Nightmare situation"
item.description: More than 700 buildings in the Spokane area have been destroyed, and another 400 have yet to be assessed, officials said Monday as three fires burned in the area.

item.title: Justice Dept. moves to dismiss Jan. 6 class action lawsuit
item.description: The Justice Department argued that the Jan. 6, 2021, rioters had until Jan. 6, 2023, to sue the federal government under the Federal Tort Claims Act, missing the deadline to file a lawsuit by over two years.

item.title: Senate pushes ahead with plan to fund government through midterms
item.description: The Senate is moving ahead with a plan to keep the government funded and avoid another shutdown before the midterm elections.

item.title: 8/3: CBS Evening News
item.description: Spokane wildfires force thousands to evacuate; Michigan reports two cyclosporiasis deaths.

item.title: Trump says oil companies should cut gas prices after making "too much money"
item.description: President Trump said U.S. oil companies made "too much money" from high oil prices. "I'm not happy about it," he added.

item.title: Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie case contradicted himself on ransom note
item.description: Investigators in the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie released two ransom notes, including one contradicting what the Arizona sheriff overseeing the case told CBS News.

item.title: Federal workers sour on government work, decrying eroding job security
item.description: Nearly two-thirds of current and retired U.S. government workers said they wouldn't re-enter public service, according to a recent survey.
